title: plugin-11: Layer content from a ViewNode + paint and input through the layer stack
summary: The layer registry ships with native content only. Its own comments say the ViewNode path (plugins) and paint/input wiring land later — this is that work.
description:
Transferred from docs/surface-compositor.md §9 on 2026-07-26, before that file was deleted. §§1–8 of it are IMPLEMENTED; §9 was marked DRAFT and is now built. **Updated 2026-08-12** — the original plugin-11 work has landed and the phase now carries the exposé that was built on it.

═══ WHAT SHIPPED — the layer stack (the phase's original scope) ═══
`heca/src/chrome/layers.rs` (1150 lines): `LayerBand` (semantic z bands, no magic numbers), `LayerKind::{Persistent, OnDemand}`, `ShowLayer`/`HideLayer`/`ToggleLayer`, and — the part §9 said would land later — **`LayerContent::{Native(Box<dyn Component>), View(ViewNode)}`** :208, realized through the one bridge (`chrome/realize.rs`). Layers paint in stack order and input routes to the active or modal layer (T336). `add_layer` returns a stable `LayerId` a plugin can hold.

The migration order from §9 is complete:
1. ~~Introduce the stack, register the existing surfaces, hints read it~~ — DONE.
2. ~~Convert the confirm dialog to a layer with hintable buttons~~ — DONE (T320), as an `OverlayHost::open_modal` with a ViewNode body and actions, not a bespoke modal.
3. ~~`ShowLayer` on-demand layers → the first native exposé~~ — DONE (T327's first half; its **exit sequencing**, fade over shrink, is the open remainder and waits on a layer's lifetime following the whole exit).
4. ~~The ViewNode content path → plugins add layers~~ — DONE (T339).

⚠️ **The KeyHint half of §9 is obsolete as written.** It described `collect_hint_targets` finding subtrees carrying `.hint_target(...)`. That API is **deleted**: `HintTargetRegistry`, `HintTargets`, `HintTargetId`, `Base::hint_target` and `named_press` were removed by F004/P084/T399 under ⭐⭐ RULE ZERO, because a plugin could construct none of them. A pick is now **one line on the widget** — `KeyHint::new(w).on_peek(…)` — collected out of the laid-out tree by `heca_grid_ui::collect_peeks` and run by `fire_peek`. Nothing is registered, so nothing has to be un-registered when a tree rebuilds. Do not reintroduce any of the deleted names.

═══ WHAT THE PHASE IS NOW — the exposé ═══
The first real layer is the **exposé** (`heca/src/chrome/expose.rs`, 2028 lines): a bird's-eye of every workspace, one row each, with a `CardGrid` cursor, surface-scoped delete keys (T416) and the open/close zoom effect. It is where the layer stack is proven, and where the remaining tasks are:

- **T417** — the layer stack becomes the surface TREE: z is a path, not a band.
- **T418** — the map's hover behaviour. The reveal now follows the **keyboard**, never the pointer (`CardGrid::reveal_state()` + `Row::reveal_when`), which Antonio confirmed. Two reported symptoms — the animation "is strange", a card is hard to click — are **still unconfirmed**, and may be consequences of the reveal loop that is now fixed. Check before changing anything.
- **T419** — the fit: the zoom is computed from the session's extents, not configured. Shipped in `4eb3136` as `fit_zoom`, and **superseded by T420**, which deletes it: under shares there is no zoom to compute.
- **T420** — split `map()` into components: `ExposeGrid` / `WorkspaceRow` / `ColumnCard` / `PaneCard`, **beside the surface** in `heca/src/chrome/expose/`, sized by **shares** (`Length::Pct` of one shared denominator, `grow` weights) with **no pixel scale anywhere**. This is the phase's centre of gravity — see its own description and the phase handoff.
- **T421** — the map is laggy with many panes (26 across 3 workspaces), worst on open/close. Prime suspect, **unmeasured**: `layout_layers` (`chrome/mod.rs`) recomputes a full `LayoutEngine::compute` over every visible layer each frame with no dirty check. Second: the frosted backdrop's full-screen blur pass per animation frame. **Measure first.**

═══ THE DECISIONS THAT GOVERN THE REMAINING WORK (Antonio, 2026-08-12) ═══
- **Components, Flutter/SwiftUI style**: *"reason in terms of Components that encapsulate their internal logic and are reusable. Like in React but write code Flutter/SwiftUI style."* A surface is components, never one function that draws a picture.
- **They live beside their surface** (`heca/src/chrome/expose/`) and move up to `heca/src/components/` when a second surface needs them.
- **Every size is a share; nothing is a pixel.** The exposé's `map()` computed a zoom and emitted `Length::Px(col.width * zoom)` — which is taking over the layout engine's job, and then owning every term (window, overlay margin, panel padding, card gaps, row count, row heights, scroll centring). Seven attempts, six wrong, each missing a different term.
- **The zoom EFFECT stays.** `effects::Zoom` + `LayerRegistry::set_zoom` (with `PaintCx::with_scale` underneath) is the open/close animation and is already generic for any layer including a plugin's. Only `overview_zoom` / `overview_scale` — the *fit* scale — goes.
- **Measure before fixing.** Six wrong guesses in one day; instrumenting named the cause in one round, every time.

═══ THE INVARIANTS THAT MUST SURVIVE (§6 of the deleted file) ═══
- NO hardcoded z or levels anywhere. z is tree position; occluders come from real layout geometry.
- Buttons NEVER declare a layer. A button inherits its layer from the surface it is mounted in.
- The active context is moved ONLY by context surfaces (exposé, modal) — never by zoom, scroll or provider selection.
- Occlusion is decided by draw order plus geometry, not by the coarse level.
- Overlays and modals are children of their opener, and exclusive when modal.
- ONE rule for visibility. If you are special-casing a surface's hints, the surface is mis-modelled — fix the model, do not add a filter.

═══ BUILD ON, DO NOT DUPLICATE ═══
`OverlayHost` is NOT a second stack — it is built ON this one. `open_modal` realizes the ViewNode body plus its action buttons into a native tree, pushes it as a Modal-band layer, and resolves the returned result when a button's intent fires. Its overlays ARE layers here.

═══ VERIFICATION ═══
Layering, paint order, hint visibility and the map are all **visible** behaviour. Green tests are not verification: Antonio drives every visual check, and green tests found none of the exposé's seven failures.

tasks.title: ShowLayer / HideLayer on-demand layers → a first native exposé
tasks.description:
Migration step 3. `ShowLayer(id)` makes an OnDemand layer visible and active, so the base context goes dormant when it is a context switch. A keybinding maps to it like any action, so it is rebindable and reachable from mouse and RPC.

## 🔴 STATE — 2026-08-12. All four items BUILT; three driven; one thing left in item 1.

`prefix+Tab` opens it; Enter/Space/click choose a pane; Escape/`q`/`Ctrl+q` close it.

| # | item | state |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | zoom in/out instead of the fade | ✅ built — **but its exit cannot sequence the shrink before the fade** (below) |
| 2 | floating panes drawn | ✅ built + driven |
| 3 | `preferred_height` respected | ✅ built; **not yet driven** with unequal stacked panes |
| 4 | `x` / `r` / `d` delete from the map | ✅ built + driven ("seems to work") |

### 1 — the zoom (`PaintCx::with_scale` + `effects::Zoom` + `LayerRegistry::set_zoom`)

Reusable, per Antonio: *"I expect they to be reusable APIs for other components and plugins."* The
paint transform scales geometry **and** font size, radius, border width, glow/shadow and clip rects;
the effect is a sibling of `Fade`; the layer declares it like `set_fade_out`. Any layer or plugin can
use all three.

**Direction: it GROWS IN and shrinks away** — `[settings] overview_zoom_from`, default `0.8`. Antonio
drove big→small (niri's reading, 1.3 and 2.0) and rejected both: *"it should go from smaller to big,
the opposite when exiting."* The setting spans both, so it is one number, not a code change.

⚠️ **Left to do: the exit plays the fade over the shrink.** `Fade::delay` and
`LayerRegistry::set_fade_out_after` were built for it and **reverted** — a layer is retired when the
*fade* finishes, so delaying the fade left the cards on screen after the map had gone. Sequencing an
exit needs a layer's lifetime to follow the **whole** exit, not the fade alone. Both APIs remain in
the library and are correct; nothing uses the delay.

### 2, 3, 4 — what they are

- **Floats** are drawn at their own rect over the strip, stacked with `Grid` (one cell, offset by a
  margin — `docs/widgets.md` → "Placing a widget at an app-chosen rect"), and are **one more column
  of cells** so the cursor reaches them. ⚠️ The strip must **stretch inside its cell**: carrying
  `align_self(Start)` there collapsed every card to a 7px sliver.
- **Pane heights** come from `Column::pane_sizes` (the layout's resolved answer), so a stack dragged
  out of balance is drawn out of balance. Columns also gained a `Spacing::Sm` gap.
- **Delete** is the card's own `on_text_input` handler dispatching `close_pane_by_id` /
  `delete_column` / `delete_workspace` through the ActionRegistry. `x` = pane, `r` = column,
  `d` = workspace — `r`, because `x` and `X` are the same *key* and differ only as typed text.
  Nothing was added to `WidgetIntent` or `ActionPolicy`; the confirm arrives with the action.
  Deleting hands the cursor to the next card in the row **first**, since afterwards the neighbour
  cannot be found.

### Five bugs it uncovered, all OUTSIDE the exposé — fixed, do not re-fix here

Key **releases** were discarded by the window loop · `add_named` promoted a rebuilt layer above
newer ones · input and painting disagreed about which layer is in front · **`close_pane_by_id`
searched only the active workspace** (the real cause of "delete does nothing in the second row") ·
a visible layer was never rebuilt when the session changed. Each has a test or a source lint. Found
by instrumenting the whole chain **after three speculative fixes failed** — reach for the trace
first.

### Settled about the map — do not "restore fidelity" to niri

Antonio overrode niri after seeing it (2026-08-05): **centre the CARD THE CURSOR IS ON**, both axes,
unclamped. `RevealWindow` and `Component::reveal_rect` were reverted; do not reintroduce them. No
workspace-name gutter. Zoom and gap come from `LayoutOptions` / `[settings]`, **never constants in
`expose.rs`**.

### The map's cursor

`AppState::expose_cursor_ws` records **which row** the cursor is on, so a rebuild restores it there;
`expose_cursor_per_ws` is still the per-workspace memory used when the map opens fresh.

## ✅ DECIDED 2026-08-04 — how a plugin updates a layer it already owns

**Signals — the plugin never resends the tree.** The mechanism is **P085(F003)/T360** (`58SE7`): a
`(mount, key) → Signal<PropValue>` map on `SharedChromeState`, plus a `ViewNode` that can name a
value key instead of a literal, so the realized widget binds the signal and updates **in place**. The
prop spelling is decided: a `bindings: Map<PropName, String>` map beside `events`. Both
`PropValue::Text("@key")` and `PropValue::Binding(String)` were rejected. **Rejected with reasons:**
*replace on update* (`update_view`) — throws the retained tree away, so caret, selection, scroll,
focus and `FormBindings` die with it; **do not add `update_view` to `LayerRegistry`**. *Diff and
reconcile* — no precedent here, largest thing in the plugin path, not until something demands it.
*Immutable layers in v1* — Antonio went to the signal model directly. Full reasoning in T360; do not
re-ask.

T327 needs a **native** exposé, which updates nothing, so nothing here is blocked by T360.

## Related tasks opened by this work

**T416** (surface-scoped keybindings — `prefix+/` currently lights hints on the sidebar *underneath*
the map) and **T417** (the layer stack becomes the surface tree), both on this phase.
**T415** (F006/P031) — config reload is a hand-written list.

---
**Completion summary:**
DONE 2026-08-20, commits 99d1ab4 + 4c8cb70. Driven and confirmed by Antonio: "T327 looks ok. pane height respect the real columns and pane height. Close it everything looks good."

All four items built AND driven:
1. zoom in/out instead of the fade — built + driven (its exit sequencing was the last open piece)
2. floating panes drawn — built + driven
3. `preferred_height` respected — built + DRIVEN 2026-08-20 (the outstanding "not yet driven" item; Antonio confirmed unequal stacked panes draw in proportion)
4. `x` / `r` / `d` delete from the map — built + driven

═══ THE LAST ITEM — the exit ═══
Parked 2026-08-12: the exit could not sequence the shrink before the fade, because a layer was
retired when its FADE finished, so delaying the fade left the cards on screen after the map had
gone. That needed a layer's lifetime to follow the WHOLE exit — T417's territory, landed 99d1ab4.

`DynamicLayer::is_leaving()` (fade running OR zoom leaving) is now what `is_active`, the visibility
end, the retirement `retain` and both `hide`/`remove` gates read. So `Fade::delay` /
`set_fade_out_after` — built and reverted a week ago — are usable, and the map's dissolve RIDES its
shrink, lagging by a SHARE of it (`ZOOM_IN * FADE_LAG`) rather than a second duration that could
drift out of step. `FADE_OUT` is `ZOOM_IN`, same reason.

═══ THREE BUGS, ALL FOUND BY TRACING THE FRAME — never by reasoning ═══
Antonio reported a fast flash just before the map vanished. THREE diagnoses by inspection (the
layer render pass, the overlay band, a missing frame) were each eliminated by an env-gated trace
(`HECA_TRACE_LAYERS`) printing per-frame `any_visible / scene cmds / band segments / each layer's
own op + scale`. The trace named it in one round, as it has every time on this phase:

  op=0.190 scale=0.801 leaving=true
  op=0.110 scale=1.000 leaving=true   <- the flash
  op=0.030 scale=1.000 leaving=true

1. `Zoom::amount` rested at 1.0. Not running => life size — but the fade outlasts the shrink, so for
   the last frames the zoom was finished while the surface was still visible at a tenth opacity, and
   the cards snapped back to full size as they faded. A finished LEAVE now rests at `from`.
   `enter`/`cancel` clear `leaving`, so only a completed exit is affected, and every surface with a
   zoom-out gets it. (heca-grid-ui/src/effects.rs)
2. A rebuild resurrected a surface mid-exit. `show` cancelled the fade unconditionally; it already
   computed `arriving` and used it for the zoom, and the fade now reads the same flag. The exposé
   hits this on the ordinary path — it dismisses itself and THEN focuses the pane you chose, and
   focusing rebuilds the map.
3. Nothing requested the frame that paints an absence. Both effects report done on the tick that
   ends an exit, so no further frame was asked for and the last one drawn still showed the surface
   faintly. `LayerRegistry::tick` now returns true on that frame, and on the frame a doomed layer is
   dropped. The test `removing_a_fading_layer_waits_for_the_fade` had the bug written into it as
   `!reg.tick(..)`.

Fix 2 was first written as a guard at the exposé call site and REJECTED by Antonio: "don't make fix
hardcoding code around, they should be centralized". Both 1 and 2 are framework fixes; the call site
is one plain line.

═══ VERIFICATION ═══
heca 565 / 0 · heca-grid-ui 236 / 0 · clippy clean. Instrumentation removed.
Regression tests `re_showing_a_leaving_layer_does_not_cancel_its_exit` and
`a_finished_leave_rests_at_from_not_back_at_life_size` were each verified to FAIL without their fix.

═══ STILL OPEN, NOT THIS TASK ═══
The map is slow with >20 panes (Antonio, 2026-08-19) — that is T421, and it is UNMEASURED. Do not
guess: instrument `layout_layers` (a full `LayoutEngine::compute` over every visible layer each
frame, no dirty check) and the frosted backdrop's per-frame full-screen blur first.

tasks.title: Paint and route input through the layer stack
tasks.description:
Today only hint visibility reads the stack. Draw layers in stack order and route input to the active or modal layer. The invariants must survive: no hardcoded z (z is tree position), buttons never declare a layer (they inherit it from their surface), the active context moves only for context surfaces — never for zoom, scroll or provider selection.

---
**Completion summary:**
Closed 2026-08-04 by a reconciliation pass — **the layer stack is laid out, painted and input-routed.**

- **Layout, every frame:** `heca/src/chrome/mod.rs::layout_layers` runs `LayoutEngine::compute` on each visible layer root, so layer children get real measured bounds rather than hand-placed ones.
- **Paint in stack order:** driven from the registry's ordering (`LayerBand` + `visible_roots_mut`), not from a hardcoded z — the invariant this task named.
- **Input:** `dispatch_modal_pointer` (`chrome/mod.rs:1271`) delivers pointer events to the top modal layer and returns `true` so "every caller stops there and nothing leaks to" what is beneath. `top_modal` and `content_covered` answer which layer owns the context; keys reach an open overlay through the keymap and the widget's own `overlay_active` capture.
- **Hints read the stack** through `collect_hint_targets(layer.root.as_ref())` (`:2185`).

The invariants held: z is tree position, buttons inherit their surface's layer rather than declaring one, and the active context moves only for context surfaces.

Live proof beyond the tests: the command palette (P092/T393) mounts as an `Overlay`-band `OnDemand` layer, is laid out each frame, captures the keyboard while open, and occludes what is behind it.

**Not re-verified visually as part of this pass** — it is exercised constantly by the palette, dropdowns and the confirm prompt, which Antonio drives regularly.

tasks.title: Add LayerContent with the View(ViewNode) arm
tasks.description:
`heca/src/chrome/layers.rs` has `LayerBand` and `LayerKind` but no `LayerContent` — a layer holds a native tree and nothing can hand it a description. Add `LayerContent::{Native(Box<dyn Component>), View(ViewNode)}` and realize the View arm through the ONE bridge (heca/src/chrome/realize.rs). Occluder comes from the realized tree's laid-out bounds — NEVER hardcoded.

---
**Completion summary:**
Done 2026-08-04. `heca/src/chrome/layers.rs` + `heca/src/chrome/overlay.rs`.

## What shipped

- **`LayerContent`** with both arms: `Native(Box<dyn Component>)` and `View { node, realized }`. `DynamicLayer.root` became `content: LayerContent`, with `root()` / `root_mut()` accessors so every consumer is arm-agnostic.
- **`LayerRegistry::add_view(band, kind, modal, covers_content, node, realized)`** — the View-arm constructor, mirroring `add`.
- **`chrome::overlay::open_view_layer(state, band, kind, modal, covers_content, node)`** — the host entry point. Realizes through the **one** bridge (`super::realize` → `heca_view_realize::realize`) with the same boundary `build_modal_root` uses: a `ViewHintTargets` sink so the described tree's buttons are KeyHint-reachable, and an emitter that wraps the model's own `Intent` into `InteractionIntent::View` at the edge.

## Design decision — the View arm keeps BOTH the node and the realized tree

The task's literal signature was `View(ViewNode)`. It is `View { node, realized }` instead, for two reasons:

1. **A registry cannot realize.** `realize(node, theme, emit, hints, forms)` needs the theme, an intent emitter, the hint sink and the form bindings; `LayerRegistry` is plain data on `AppState` and holds none of them. So the caller realizes and hands both over — which is why `open_view_layer` exists at all.
2. **Keeping only the tree would throw the description away.** The node is the source of truth a theme reload or a plugin update re-realizes from; the tree is what the host lays out, paints and hint-walks. `LayerContent::node()` exposes it, and the test asserts it survives realization.

## The occluder invariant holds

Nothing is hardcoded and nothing was added: `active_hint_targets` (`heca/src/chrome/mod.rs:2182`) reads `layer.root().base().bounds`, so a View layer's occluder is its **realized tree's laid-out bounds** by construction — it goes through the same accessor as a native one.

## Verification

1151 tests, clippy 0 warnings. New test `a_view_layer_behaves_like_any_other_and_keeps_its_description`: a described layer sorts by band beside a native one, declares coverage the same way, keeps its `ViewNode`, and a native layer offers no description — the arms are not interchangeable.

## Follow-on

`open_view_layer` has **no caller yet** — it is a seam, which is why `layers.rs` still carries `#![allow(dead_code)]`. Its first consumer is **P082(F003)/T327** (`ShowLayer` / `HideLayer` actions → the native exposé): the registry's `show()`/`hide()` already exist and are documented as "`ShowLayer` dispatches here", but no `WmAction` reaches them.

Not verified visually — nothing renders through this path until T327 gives it a caller.

tasks.title: Surface-scoped keybindings: the active context owns the keyboard, and hints/menus follow it
tasks.description:
**Read `docs/surface-compositor.md` §2, §3, §5 and §6 first** — recovered from git 2026-08-12 after being deleted in `3d71092` under a commit message claiming its content had been transferred. This task is that design, applied to input.

# The defect

**While the exposé is open, the app underneath is still being driven.**

- `prefix+j` / `prefix+k` change the focused pane in the session behind the map.
- **`prefix+/` picks targets that are not on screen.** Antonio, 2026-08-12: *"prefix+/ acts under the
  exposé. I don't see the hint but after prefix+/ I type `a` (or a random letter) and see the sidebar
  changing focus, from the little space around the exposé."* The letters are **invisible** — drawn
  beneath the map or outside it — while the targets are **live**, so a keystroke acts on a surface
  the user cannot see and has no warning about. Worse than visibly wrong letters.
- `prefix+p`, `prefix+e` and the rest of the app's bindings all run.

Antonio: *"In the overlay we should not be able to do a lot of prefix+key things… Each overlay should
declare its own keybinding and actions."*

# Why it happens — one flag answering two questions

`docs/surface-compositor.md` §2 keeps **two orthogonal mechanisms** apart:

1. **Coarse — context activation.** `current_index` points at the active context surface. Opening a
   modal sets it: *"it's exclusive → everything beneath goes dormant."*
2. **Fine — geometric occlusion.** Within the eligible set, a target is hidden iff a higher-z
   surface's occluder covers its centre.

`domain_for` (`heca/src/app/interaction.rs:212`) asks the **fine** question to decide the **coarse**
one: it calls `chrome::content_covered(state)` — a fact about what is painted over — to decide
`Domain::Overlay`. The exposé declares `covers_content: false` because that is geometrically true
(you can see the panes, and the hint resolver needs that), and by doing so it also, accidentally,
says "the base context is still live". One flag, two questions, opposite answers needed.

§6's invariant names it: *"If you find yourself special-casing a surface's hints, the surface is
mis-modelled — fix the model, don't add a filter."*

# What to build

## 1. The coarse gate is "is a context surface active", not "does something cover the content"

`domain_for` returns `Domain::Overlay` while a **modal** layer is active
(`LayerRegistry::top_modal_index` exists and already orders by band). Coverage goes back to meaning
only what it says. The exposé keeps `covers_content: false` and still makes the base context dormant.

## 2. What survives is `ActionPolicy::Global` — the existing classification

`Domain::Overlay` already permits only `Global`. Two actions must be **reclassified**, being
surface-agnostic by nature and acting on whichever context is live:

- `open_context_menu` (`prefix+>`)
- the leader/hint picker (`prefix+/`)

`reload_config` and `close_overlay` already are. `focus_down`, `command_palette`, `focus_dock` and
the rest stay as they are and are refused while a context is up — the wanted behaviour. **`prefix+e`
is not global**: it is the workspaces component's own `global_focus`
(`keybindings.default.toml:681`), and it should not work from inside the map.

⚠️ **The map's own intents must keep working**: `close_pane_by_id`, `delete_column`,
`delete_workspace`, `FocusPaneThenAction` and `CloseOverlay` are dispatched by the exposé's own tree
with `InteractionSource::Keyboard`. If the domain rule refuses them the deletes break (only just made
to work — T327 item 4). Either give a layer's own tree its own `InteractionSource`, **or** judge by
the surface the intent came from. Antonio's constraint: *"it should be valid for all overlays… but
each overlay might use its own actions and keybindings so we risk blocking future actions."* It
cannot be a fixed allow-list — it has to be the action's own declared policy plus where the intent
came from.

## 3. `prefix+/` collects only the active context's targets

`chrome::active_peek_targets` walks the chrome tree, every `state.pane_headers` tree and **every
visible layer**. Per §3 the eligible set is *"`current_index` plus its visible, non-blocking
descendants"* — everything below the active context is suppressed. That filter is missing, which is
why a letter picks a sidebar row while the map is up. Same rule for the context menu.

**Check the drawing too**: even for eligible targets, the keycaps must paint above the active
surface. A target whose letter cannot be seen is not pickable in any useful sense — the invisible
letters above are half of what made this hard to notice.

## 4. Surface-scoped keys: `[[keys.surface]]`

A dock and an overlay are the same thing to the keyboard. `[[keys.component]]`
(`keybindings.default.toml:676`) already carries the two tiers — `global_focus = "prefix+e"` reaches
the workspaces dock from outside; `cursor_up` / `activate_selected` / `create_workspace` apply only
while it holds the keyboard. Generalise to **`[[keys.surface]]`** with `name` = the surface id
(`workspaces`, `expose`, a plugin's), keeping `[[keys.component]]` as an accepted spelling so
existing configs keep working. The shape Antonio sketched:

```toml
[[keys.surface]]
name         = "expose"
global_focus = "prefix+Tab"
dismiss      = "q,Escape"
delete_pane  = "x"
```

Resolution: the surface holding the keyboard first (shadowing, the way a neovim floating window's
buffer-local mappings shadow the global map), then the app's, then filtered by the action's policy.

This also removes today's oddity that the exposé's `x` / `r` / `d` are **literals in Rust**
(`heca/src/chrome/expose.rs::delete_keys`) rather than bindings a user can rebind.

## 5. A plugin needs nothing host-private

`ActionMeta.policy` already exists (`heca/src/actions.rs:2007`) beside `args`, `confirm` and `icon`,
and `register_dynamic` registers a name-keyed action. So a plugin declares its actions' policies at
registration and its keys as its own surface layer. **Verify this end to end** — it is the Rule Zero
test for this task.

**A binding is never "global" — the action is.** `[keys]` "global" means *typed without the prefix*;
`ActionPolicy::Global` means *allowed in every domain*. It belongs on the action because the same
action is reached from a key, a menu entry, the palette, a button and RPC; on the binding, the other
four surfaces would have no answer.

# Verification (Antonio drives)

Open the exposé: `prefix+j/k` do nothing · `prefix+/` shows letters **only on the map's cards**, and
typing one acts only there · `prefix+>` opens the map's own menu · `prefix+Shift+r` still reloads ·
`ctrl+j/k` still move the map's cursor · `x`/`r`/`d` still delete. Then the same with a dock focused,
to confirm nothing regressed there.

tasks.title: The layer stack becomes the surface TREE — z is a path, not a band
tasks.description:
**Read `docs/surface-compositor.md` §2 ("The surface tree"), §3, §5 and §6 first** — recovered from git 2026-08-12. The tree is the recorded design; what we shipped is a flattened approximation of it.

# Current state vs the design

`heca/src/chrome/layers.rs` holds a **flat `Vec<DynamicLayer>`** ordered by a `LayerBand` enum
(`Background < Content < Floating < Overlay < Modal`) plus insertion order within a band.

The design says (§2):

> **z is the position in this tree — never a stored number.** A surface's z-path is the chain of
> sibling indices from the root to it (`[4,0]`). Ordering is lexicographic on the path, which equals
> a pre-order traversal, which equals paint order.
>
> - a **child is above its parent**, so a modal is above its opener;
> - later siblings are above earlier ones;
> - inserting "in the middle" is `Vec::insert` at the right sibling index — no float fragility, no
>   renumbering by hand.

§5: *"a modal opened from the exposé is a **child of the exposé** — it automatically sits above it
and, being modal, becomes the new `current_index`."*

**A band is a stored z.** §6's first invariant is *"No hardcoded z / levels anywhere"*, and a
five-variant enum every caller picks from is exactly that, one step removed.

# Why it is worth doing — the bugs it removes as a class

Both layer bugs found on 2026-08-11 are "z is stored/implicit" bugs, not incidents:

1. **`add_named` removed-and-re-appended**, so rebuilding a layer promoted it above anything opened
   since — the confirm dialog opened over the exposé, the map rebuilt, and the click on "Close" went
   to the map. Fixed by replacing in place.
2. **Input and painting disagreed about which layer is in front**: painting sorted by band,
   `top_modal_*` took the last one added and ignored the band. Fixed by giving input the same order.

In a tree neither is expressible: a rebuild replaces a node, and there is exactly one order.

**The deciding argument is plugins**, which is what F003 is for. A plugin opens a panel; the panel
opens a modal; the panel closes. The modal must sit above *that* panel and must go with it. In a flat
list that is bookkeeping every caller can get wrong; in the tree it is free.

# What to build

- `SurfaceId` + a tree of nodes, each with `parent` and ordered `children` (§7 sketches the target
  API). Order = pre-order traversal; **delete `LayerBand`** and the `rank()` beside it.
- **`current_index`** — the active context surface (§2's coarse mechanism). Opening a context sets
  it; closing restores the previous. This is what T416 needs, and doing that task first against the
  flat model means writing the gate twice.
- **Occluder from real laid-out geometry** (§2), never a constant — already true of
  `active_peek_targets`, keep it.
- Migrate the three readers: `chrome::mod.rs`'s paint pass (`visible_back_to_front`),
  `top_modal_*` / `dispatch_modal_pointer`, and `active_peek_targets`.
- Keep `add_named`'s in-place replacement semantics (a re-registration keeps its **place, its
  visibility and any animation in flight** — 2026-08-11), and the `heca.` owner-prefix namespacing.

# Sequencing

**Do it as part of P035 (plugin-05, the overlay host) or immediately before T416**, not after: the
overlay host is the code that first creates parent/child overlays, and T416's coarse gate is
`current_index`. Building either against the flat `Vec` means rewriting it when the tree lands.

# Edge cases

- **Bands are load-bearing today** for "a `Modal`-band layer covers the content even if it says
  otherwise" (`a_modal_band_layer_covers_the_content_even_if_it_says_otherwise`). In the tree that
  becomes "a modal context is exclusive", which is §2's own wording — make sure the test moves rather
  than being deleted.
- **A dissolving layer must not hold input** (`is_active`), and removal waits for the fade — keep
  both, and note that the exposé's exit cannot sequence its zoom before its fade until a node's
  lifetime follows the whole exit rather than the fade alone (found 2026-08-11).
- Existing tests to carry over: `band_orders_front_to_back` (becomes path ordering),
  `input_goes_to_the_front_most_band_not_the_last_one_added`,
  `re_registering_a_layer_does_not_promote_it_above_a_newer_one`,
  `re_showing_a_visible_layer_does_not_restart_its_zoom`.

---
**Completion summary:**
DONE 2026-08-19, commit 99d1ab4. Driven by Antonio ("works").

═══ WHAT SHIPPED ═══
- `LayerBand` + `rank()` DELETED. `DynamicLayer.band` → `parent: Option<LayerId>`.
- `LayerRegistry::z_path(id)` — the chain of sibling indices from the root. Ordering is
  lexicographic on it = pre-order = paint order. A child is above its parent, a later sibling above
  an earlier one, and nobody writes a z.
- `visible_front_to_back` and `top_modal_index` both sort by that one order, so paint and input
  cannot name different layers any more (the 2026-08-11 bug is not expressible).
- `current` + `context_stack` on the registry = the coarse `current_index` of §2. A modal that
  arrives takes the context; hiding/removing hands it back. `open_modal`, `open_dropdown` and
  `insert_menu_layer` pass `state.layers.current()`, so a modal raised from the exposé is a CHILD of
  the exposé with no caller saying so. The exposé itself mounts at `None` (base context).

═══ THE ONE THING THE RECORD DID NOT SETTLE ═══
`content_covered` used `band == Modal` to force coverage even when a layer declared
`covers_content: false`. That override cannot become `l.modal`: the exposé is `modal: true` and must
NOT cover (it is a map of the panes — acting on the one you see is the point), which the test
`an_overlay_that_takes_the_keyboard_can_still_declare_it_covers_nothing` pins.

Checked both real call sites — `open_modal` and `insert_menu_layer` — and BOTH already pass
`covers_content: true`. The override was guarding a call site since fixed. So coverage is now the
declaration alone, and `a_modal_band_layer_covers_the_content_even_if_it_says_otherwise` moved to
`coverage_is_what_the_surface_declared_not_what_its_place_implies` rather than being deleted.

═══ ALSO IN THIS COMMIT (found by Antonio driving) ═══
The top bar's two sidebar toggles swapped their `prefix+/` letters on every toggle: both flip their
glyph with the sidebar state, so with no key their identity was the glyph's NAME, and collapsing the
left made both derive `arrow_line_right` — one bare, one `[1]`, decided by document order.

FIXED IN THE FRAMEWORK, not at the call site (Antonio was emphatic; a call-site fix was written
first and rejected): `nav::identity_of` now resolves **through transparent wrappers**
(`through_wrappers` — no key, no action, exactly one visible child). The picker addresses the node
that DECLARED the hint, which is the `KeyHint` wrapper, while the key belongs on the control inside
it. Without this every author wrapping a control would have had to key the wrapper. The call site is
now one ordinary line: `IconButton::new(..).key(action_name)`.

The same descent backs T444's warning (`item_of`), which had been blind to any control behind a
wrapper — which is why nothing printed while the bug was live.

═══ TESTS ═══
`band_orders_front_to_back` → `z_is_a_path_so_a_child_is_in_front_of_its_parent_and_a_later_sibling_of_an_earlier`.
`input_goes_to_the_front_most_band_not_the_last_one_added` → `..._front_most_surface_...`, expressed
as parenthood. New: `an_overlay_sits_above_its_opener_not_above_the_newest_layer` (the plugin case),
`the_active_context_follows_the_modal_surfaces`, `a_control_behind_wrappers_is_still_an_item`,
`the_sidebar_toggles_keep_their_identity_when_a_sidebar_is_toggled`. The four carry-over tests the
task named all still pass. Both new regression tests were verified to FAIL without their fix.

heca 564 passed / 0 failed · heca-grid-ui 234 / 0 · clippy clean.

═══ UNBLOCKS ═══
T327's remaining item — the exposé's exit cannot sequence the shrink before the fade — was parked
waiting for a layer's lifetime to follow the WHOLE exit rather than the fade alone. That is this
task's territory and it is now available.

NOT built here (never in scope): the panes, the chrome root and the floats are still painted outside
the registry, so the tree's root children are the registry's layers rather than §2's named surfaces.

tasks.title: The map's hover behaviour — the autocentring loop, the animation, and a card that is hard to click
tasks.description:
**Antonio, driving, 2026-08-12 (second report, after T416 landed):** *"the animation when hovering the cards and the autocentering behavior need deeper review because its strange. mouse hover is hard to click."*

**First report, 2026-08-12:** *"when there is only one workspace in the exposé, moving hover with the mouse causes the map to slide right and left to center the hovered pane, but this brings it too far from the mouse."*

Three symptoms were reported. **Two are now closed** (Antonio, 2026-08-13). One remains, and it is the one that was never diagnosed.

| # | Symptom | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Hovering slides the map to centre the card, moving it away from the pointer | ✅ **CLOSED** — gone by construction |
| 2 | The hover animation itself "is strange" | 🔴 **OPEN — the whole of this task now** |
| 3 | A card is hard to click | ✅ **CLOSED** — Antonio, 2026-08-13: *"hard to click no more"* |

# 1 and 3 — closed, and why they cannot come back the same way

**The fix (landed in `4eb3136`):** the reveal follows the **keyboard**, never the pointer — `CardGrid::reveal_state()` publishes "the cursor last moved by keyboard", and `Row::reveal_when(signal)` gates the card's `wants_visible`. This stays: it is a framework rule, and any list or grid that follows its cursor has the same loop waiting.

**And T420 removed the loop's other half.** The map is built out of shares of the window, so it always fits, so **both `ScrollRegion`s in the map are deleted**. Antonio, 2026-08-13: *"since we moved to Flex there is no more scroll."* Hovering a card cannot move the map — by construction rather than by a gate.

The hard-to-click report went with it: it was a consequence of a map that moved under the pointer, and the pointer no longer has anything to chase.

# 2 — THE OPEN ITEM: the animation "is strange"

⚠️ **Undiagnosed, and it must not be guessed at.** The scroll animation it was probably blamed on is gone, so whatever remains is something else. The 2026-08-11 lesson applies exactly: three speculative fixes, two of them real defects, the app still broken until one traced run found the cause.

**What is still animated, and therefore the only two candidates:**

1. **The card's own cursor visuals** — `Row`'s highlight/scale transition as the cursor moves between cards.
2. **The layer's open/close `effects::Zoom`** — `LayerRegistry::set_zoom` + `overview_zoom_from`, with `PaintCx::with_scale` underneath. Note this is the zoom **effect**, which T420 deliberately kept; only the *fit* scale was deleted.

**Before changing a line, get from Antonio what "strange" means here** — which of these it is, and what it looks like: does it restart, overshoot, jump, run at the wrong speed, or play when it should not? The word covered three different things last time, and two of them turned out to be the scroll loop rather than an animation at all.

Then **instrument**: a trace at the transition's start/end and at the layer's zoom set, before any fix.

# Verification (Antonio drives)

Open the map on a session with one workspace and several columns:

1. Move the mouse across the cards: **the map does not move.** ✅ confirmed
2. Watch the motion while arrowing: it starts and settles once, and does not restart or overshoot. ⬅ **this is the open one**
3. Click a card the pointer is resting on: it activates, first time. ✅ confirmed
4. Arrow with `ctrl+h/l`: the cursor moves and the map stays put — nothing scrolls because nothing is off screen. ✅ implied by 1
5. Wheel over the map: nothing moves, and that is now correct rather than a regression. ✅ implied by 1

---
**Completion summary:**
**CLOSED 2026-08-13** — Antonio, driving the rebuilt map: *"there is no hover animation"*, *"hard to click no more"*, *"since we moved to Flex there is no more scroll."* All three reported symptoms are gone.

# The three symptoms, and what actually resolved each

| # | Symptom | Resolution |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Hovering slides the map to centre the card, moving it away from the pointer | Fixed twice over — see below |
| 2 | The hover animation "is strange" | **There is no hover animation.** The thing being described was symptom 1. |
| 3 | A card is hard to click | Gone with symptom 1 — the pointer has nothing to chase |

**Symptom 1, fixed at two levels.** First in `4eb3136`: the reveal follows the **keyboard**, never the pointer — `CardGrid::reveal_state()` publishes "the cursor last moved by keyboard" and `Row::reveal_when(signal)` gates the card's `wants_visible`. That stays, because it is a framework rule: any list or grid that follows its cursor has the same loop waiting. Then T420 removed the loop's other half — the map is built out of shares of the window, so it always fits, so **both `ScrollRegion`s are deleted**. Hovering cannot move the map by construction rather than by a gate.

**Symptom 2 was never a separate defect.** "The animation when hovering the cards… is strange" described the map sliding under the pointer, which is symptom 1. There is no hover transition on these cards. This is the third time in this phase that one word covered a different mechanism than it named — the reason the task insisted on driving before diagnosing, and the reason nothing was tuned on a guess.

# What Antonio DID find, and it is not this task

The air between cards in the top row varies by a pixel. **Measured** with a headless probe (14 equal columns in a 1900px box): gaps of 6 / 7 / 8 px, card widths of 128 or 129. Nominal air is `2 × Spacing::Xs ≈ 7px`, and each column's edges round independently because a column's width is a `Length::Pct` of the map's extent, so a fractional boundary rounds one way on the left and the other on the right.

Filed separately — it is a layout-rounding defect, not a hover behaviour, and it is not specific to the exposé: anything laying percentage-sized siblings side by side with padding for air has it.

# Verification (Antonio drove all five)

1. Move the mouse across the cards: the map does not move. ✅
2. Watch the motion while arrowing: nothing to watch — there is no hover animation. ✅
3. Click a card the pointer is resting on: activates first time. ✅
4. `ctrl+h/l`: the cursor moves, the map stays put. ✅
5. Wheel over the map: nothing moves, correctly. ✅

---
**Completion summary:**
**CLOSED 2026-08-13.** Four symptoms in the end, all resolved.

# 1–3: the hover reports (Antonio, driving)

| # | Symptom | Resolution |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Hovering slides the map to centre the card, moving it away from the pointer | Fixed twice over |
| 2 | The hover animation "is strange" | *"there is no hover animation"* — this was symptom 1 being described |
| 3 | A card is hard to click | *"hard to click no more"* — gone with symptom 1 |

**Symptom 1, fixed at two levels.** `4eb3136`: the reveal follows the **keyboard**, never the pointer (`CardGrid::reveal_state()` + `Row::reveal_when(signal)`). That stays — it is a framework rule, and any list or grid that follows its cursor has the same loop waiting. Then T420 removed the other half: the map is shares of the window, so it always fits, so **both `ScrollRegion`s are deleted**. Antonio: *"since we moved to Flex there is no more scroll."* Hovering cannot move the map by construction rather than by a gate.

⚠️ Symptom 2 was never a separate defect. One word covered a different mechanism than it named — which is why nothing was tuned before he drove it.

# 4: the uneven air between cards — THE REAL FIND

**Antonio, driving, 2026-08-13:** *"the only thing i see here is the different gap between the first 3/4 card at the top and the last."*

**Measured** (headless probe over `WorkspaceRow`, 14 equal columns in a 1900×600 box):

```
before   gaps 6 7 7 8 7 6 7 7 6 7 8 7 6      widths 128/129
after    gaps 6 6 6 6 6 6 6 6 6 6 6 6 6
```

…and with the widths a real session has (not all equal), also uniform:

```
widths  181 193 181 187 181 181 200 180 181 175
gaps      6   6   6   6   6   6   6   6   6
```

## The cause

Two facts met, neither wrong on its own:

1. **A spacing token is a fraction of the font** — `Spacing::Xs` is `0.25 ×` it (`heca-grid-ui/src/style.rs:116`), so it resolves to **half a pixel** at most font sizes.
2. **Percentage-sized siblings put their air in padding, not a gap** (`chrome/expose/column_card.rs:44`). That is deliberate and must stay: a gap is added *outside* a percentage width, so the widest row would come out at 100% plus its gaps and overflow by exactly that much.

So every boundary between two cards is made of **two paddings**, and half a pixel each side rounds in opposite directions. A ±1px error on a 7px gap is a 14% variation — exactly the size of thing an eye reads as an uneven rhythm without being able to name it.

## The fix

`heca-grid-ui/src/layout.rs` — a resolved spacing token is rounded to a whole pixel, for `padding_x`, `padding_y` **and** `gap` alike. All three are the same computation; rounding one and not the others is the kind of split that drifts where tests cannot see it.

A widget's own padding moves by at most half a pixel, which is under what the screen can draw. The rhythm *between* siblings is what is actually read.

⚠️ **This is a library change and applies to every widget using spacing tokens**, not just the map.

## Guarded by

`workspace_row.rs::the_air_between_the_columns_is_the_same_everywhere` — asserts the gaps between fourteen columns are all **equal**, not that they equal 6, so it survives a font or token change.

# Gates

Workspace green (28 binaries), clippy 0 warnings with `--all-targets --all-features`. Uncommitted on `main`.

tasks.title: The exposé fits everything on screen — the zoom is computed, not configured
tasks.description:
**Antonio, 2026-08-12:** *"is it right that some cards are shown outside the view? shouldn't we zoom out the whole area and the pane increases so that we can see them all at sight?"* — and, on the shared-zoom question: *"Ok"*.

# The defect

An exposé shows everything at once; that is what the name means. Today the map uses a **fixed** zoom (`[settings] overview_scale`, default `0.5`, read at `heca/src/chrome/expose.rs:363` as `geometry.overview_scale`) and scrolls whatever does not fit. So on a session wider than two screens the cards run off the edge and the surface stops being a map of the session and becomes a window onto part of one.

# What to build — one shared zoom, fit to the view, clamped at both ends

**One zoom for the whole map**, not one per row: Antonio chose this. It keeps the workspaces comparable in size so the map reads as one picture, where a per-row fit makes a two-pane workspace's cards huge beside a ten-pane one.

The zoom becomes computed, with `overview_scale` demoted from *the* zoom to a **maximum**:

```
fit   = min(fit_horizontal, fit_vertical)
zoom  = min(fit, overview_scale).max(floor)
```

- **`fit_horizontal`** — the widest row must fit. Everything needed is already on the model
  (`heca/src/chrome/expose.rs:80` `ExposeWorkspace`): `strip_width` is the sum of the columns
  (already resolved by the layout, never recomputed), and `viewport` is `(x, width)` — the screen.
  ⚠️ **Floats can stick out past `strip_width`**: `ExposeFloating` carries its own `x`/`w`, so the
  row's true extent is `max(strip_width, max(float.x + float.w))`.
- **`fit_vertical`** — N rows plus the gaps between them must fit. The gap is
  `viewport_h * overview_gap * zoom` (niri's tenth-of-a-screen, `expose.rs:444`), so the height is
  `zoom * viewport_h * (N + (N-1) * overview_gap)` and the fit falls out as
  `1 / (N + (N-1) * overview_gap)` — independent of the pixel height, which is the tell that it is
  the right form.
- **`floor`** — a card must stay legible. A *scale* floor does not guarantee that, because columns
  differ in width; the honest floor is a **minimum card width in logical pixels**, so
  `floor = min_card_width / narrowest_column_width`. Under it the map overflows and scrolls again,
  which is the only honest answer for thirty panes.

⚠️ **`min` then `max`, never `clamp`** — `f64::clamp` panics when `min > max`, and a user with a
small `overview_scale` and a large minimum card width is exactly that case. Legibility wins there;
say so in the doc comment.

# The setting

`overview_min_card_width` beside the other three in `LayoutOptions`
(`heca-core/src/layout/types.rs:183`, where `overview_scale` / `overview_zoom_from` / `overview_gap`
already live), fed from `heca-config/src/settings.rs` like its neighbours.

**AGENTS § 2**: a new `SettingsConfig` field that is not written into `config.default.toml` is a bug
— the default then lives only in code, invisible to the user. Add it there with a comment, and to
`README.md` beside the other overview settings. `overview_scale`'s own documentation has to change
too: it is now a **maximum**, not the zoom.

# What falls out for free

If nothing overflows, nothing scrolls — so the autocentring problem T418 addresses stops existing
in the common case rather than being suppressed. Do **not** treat that as a reason to revert T418:
a session past the floor still scrolls, and the hover loop would still be there waiting.

# Edge cases

- **One workspace, one pane** — `fit` is large, `overview_scale` caps it, so the map does not blow
  a single pane up to fill the screen.
- **An empty workspace** — `strip_width` falls back to the viewport (`expose.rs:94`), so a row of
  nothing is still a screen-shaped row and the fit is not divided by zero.
- **A workspace with no columns but floats** — the extent must still come out positive.
- The **zoom animation** on open (`set_zoom`, `overview_zoom_from`) multiplies whatever this
  resolves to; it is a separate transform and needs no change.
- `heca/src/chrome/expose.rs:995` and `:1156` assert card sizes against
  `LayoutOptions::default().overview_scale` — they will need the computed zoom instead, and that is
  the point: a test that hardcodes the old constant would pass while the map fits nothing.

# Verification (Antonio drives)

- Several workspaces, one wide with many columns: **every card is on screen**, and the widest row
  just fits.
- A small session: cards do not balloon — `overview_scale` still caps it.
- A session past the floor: cards stay legible and the map scrolls, rather than shrinking to
  slivers.
- Reload (`prefix+Shift+r`) after changing `overview_min_card_width` in `config.toml` takes effect.

---
**Completion summary:**
**Done — the goal, by a different mechanism (2026-08-13).**

The task's goal was "the exposé fits everything on screen — the zoom is computed, not configured". It shipped that way in `4eb3136` as `fit_zoom` + `overflows`, driven by Antonio with a geometry trace after four wrong corrections.

**T420 then deleted both.** Under shares there is no zoom to compute and no fit that can fail: a column is a percentage of one shared denominator, a pane and a row are `grow` weights, and taffy resolves them against whatever room the window gives. The map fits **by construction**, at every window size — which is the goal, more strongly than a computed zoom could hold it.

What replaced the arithmetic: `ExposeGrid`'s `the_whole_map_never_exceeds_the_box_it_is_given` (4 sessions × 4 window sizes, rows of unequal height), plus `a_stack_never_exceeds_the_column_it_is_given`. The seven fit tests went with `fit_zoom`.

`overview_min_card_width` — the floor this task added — is deleted end to end. `overview_zoom` / `overview_scale` survives but **no longer reaches the exposé**; see the follow-up filed about the dormant core overview mode that is now its only reader.

tasks.title: Split the exposé into components — ExposeGrid / WorkspaceRow / ColumnCard / PaneCard, sized by shares
tasks.description:
**Antonio, 2026-08-12:** *"I want you to reason in terms of Components that encapsulate their internal logic and are reusable. Like in React but write code Flutter/SwiftUI style."* — *"we need to split the expose in components. ExposeGrid, WorkspaceRow, ColumnCard, PaneCard and align them using Flex or Grid. Each component encapsulates its internal business logic, accepts properties, events and callbacks."*

# BUILT 2026-08-13 — uncommitted on `feat/palette-modes`. ⏳ AWAITING ANTONIO'S DRIVE.

Workspace tests green (517 + the rest), clippy 0 warnings with `--all-targets --all-features`. **Not verified visually** — that is the last step and it is his.

## What the surface is now

`heca/src/chrome/expose.rs` (2028 lines, one ~400-line `map()`) → `heca/src/chrome/expose/`:

| file | lines | owns |
|---|---|---|
| `mod.rs` | 557 | host wiring: `register()`, `callbacks()`, `map()` (**40 lines**), `share_v()` |
| `model.rs` | 282 | the session reduced to data (unchanged behaviour) |
| `pane_card.rs` | 356 | one pane: name, cursor/focus, delete letters, activate |
| `column_card.rs` | 145 | the panes' **vertical** shares |
| `workspace_row.rs` | 336 | the columns' **horizontal** shares + the floats' rects |
| `expose_grid.rs` | 322 | the rows' shares of the map + the cursor |
| `testing.rs` | 119 | the shared fixtures (`#[cfg(test)]`) |

Each takes properties as struct fields (Flutter-style named parameters), events/callbacks through one `ExposeCallbacks` group, and **never `&AppState`**. `PaneCard`/`ColumnCard` return their concrete widget so the parent can still size them; a boxed component has no builders left.

## The sizing, as built

- **column width** = `Pct(col.width / extent)` inside a strip of `Pct(extent / widest)`, `widest` = the widest extent in the **map**. Two levels, one denominator each; multiplied out it is `col.width / widest`, so every row is at the same scale.
- **pane height** = `share_v` (`grow` + zero base + shrink — CSS `flex: 1 1 0`).
- **row height** = `share_v(row, viewport_h + gap)`.
- **the gap** = a share too: each row's allotment includes it and the strip takes `Pct(screen_h / (screen_h + gap))`, centred, so half sits above and half below and two rows meet as one full gap. `overview_gap` keeps its meaning (a tenth of a screen) at every window size.
- **air between columns** = the ColumnCard's own `pad_x`, **not** the row's `gap` — a gap is added *outside* the width shares, so the widest row would come out at 100% + its gaps and overflow by exactly that. Padding is inside the border box. Vertically a gap is safe (`grow` divides what is left after gaps), so the panes use one.
- The only `Length::Px` left in the whole surface is the `Px(0.0)` flex base inside `share_v`.

## ⚠️ The decided float mechanism had a hole — asked, and a new library capability landed

Percentage margins **cannot** place a float. Measured, not assumed: a `Pct` margin resolves against the parent's **width on both axes** (CSS's rule; taffy implements it faithfully), so `margin_top(Pct(y / viewport_h))` silently produces the wrong number on any row that is not square. Guard: `heca-grid-ui/src/layout.rs::a_percentage_margin_resolves_against_the_parents_width_on_both_axes`.

Put to Antonio with three options; he chose **a fractional-rect builder in `heca-grid-ui`**:

- `style::Placement { left, top, width, height }` — four `Length`s, `Serialize`/`Deserialize`;
- `Layout::placement: Option<Placement>` → taffy `position: Absolute` + per-axis `inset`, overriding `width`/`height`;
- **`LayoutExt::at_rect(left, top, width, height)`** — one line, on every widget, and out of the flow so a float draws *over* the strip instead of pushing it along. The `Grid`-cell stacking trick the old map used is gone.
- The **declarative half works and is proven**, not assumed (AGENTS' "adding serde is not the same as being able to author it"): `heca-view-realize::a_description_can_place_a_node_at_a_fractional_rect` authors it as a `PropValue::Map`.
- Docs: rustdoc on the builder + `docs/widgets.md` → "Placing a widget at an app-chosen rect" now carries an `at_rect` subsection for both audiences.

## Deleted

`fit_zoom`, `overflows`, `share`, both `ScrollRegion`s in the map, `SCROLL_EASE`, the three debug traces (`expose fit:` / `expose laid out:` / `center_pad:`), the `#![allow(dead_code)]` seam allow, and `overview_min_card_width` end to end (`LayoutOptions` + `SettingsConfig` + `config.default.toml` + `startup.rs`). `SURFACE` is now actually used by `register` instead of the literal it had drifted from.

**Kept:** the zoom *effect* (`set_zoom` + `overview_zoom_from`), the model, `CardGrid`, the `[[keys.surface]]` letters, the intents, the confirm, `pane_nav_key`.

## Tests — 25 in the surface, one per component plus the one that matters

- `PaneCard` — shows its name; its cell's signal **is** its focus signal; the letters act on the pane/column/workspace it sits in; an unbound letter dispatches nothing; a real press+release click chooses it.
- `ColumnCard` — panes in proportion to their real heights; **the stack never exceeds its column**, at 1/2/3/12 panes.
- `WorkspaceRow` — columns in proportion against the map's denominator; a short row is centred; **a float lands at its own fraction on BOTH axes**; a float displaces nothing; a float past the strip's end widens the extent.
- `ExposeGrid` — ⚠️ **`the_whole_map_never_exceeds_the_box_it_is_given`**: 4 sessions × 4 window sizes, including rows of unequal height. This is the assertion that would have caught every one of the seven failures. Plus rows in proportion, the gap, one card focused at a time, the cursor walking onto a float.
- `mod.rs` — the shipped letters reach the cards; the defaults bind them; the cursor is handed on before a delete; activate and dismiss reach the grid through the overlay; no workspace label is drawn and the map is all in the overlay layer; the assembled map stays inside the window at three sizes.

Dropped with the arithmetic they tested: the seven fit tests (`the_map_zooms_out_until_the_widest_row_fits`, `a_small_session_is_capped_rather_than_magnified`, `there_is_no_minimum_card_width_by_default`, `cards_stop_shrinking_at_the_minimum_width`, `a_floor_above_the_ceiling_does_not_panic`, `the_rows_fit_stacked_with_their_gaps`, `rows_of_different_heights_are_summed_not_multiplied`) and the two centring tests.

# Verification — Antonio drives, and this is the whole of what is left

Three workspaces, ~26 panes: everything on screen at once, margins that look deliberate, the wheel moves nothing, resizing re-fits live, clicking a card the pointer rests on activates first time, and the open/close zoom still plays.

⚠️ **Expect one deliberate change in the picture**: the map now fills **both** axes independently, so a row's aspect is no longer the screen's. That is what "the margins disappear under shares" means — whichever axis used to bind left slack on the other. If it reads wrong, the fix is a decision about aspect, not about arithmetic.

---

**VERIFIED by Antonio across three themes and COMMITTED as `e7f30ad`** on `feat/palette-modes` (2026-08-13): *"now its perfect."*

Driven in the GPU app over several rounds; every defect found in the drive was fixed and re-driven — the map opening on the focused pane (T423), the card name centred, the card given a real surface so mocha's cards stopped vanishing into the scrim, the doubled left bar removed, and selection/cursor separated by kind rather than hue (T425).

Plus `LayoutExt::at_rect` + `style::Placement` in `heca-grid-ui`, `heca/src/components/` (T373), and AGENTS.md § 0b-bis (T424).

Deleted: `fit_zoom`, `overflows`, both `ScrollRegion`s, `SCROLL_EASE`, the three debug traces, `trace_layer_geometry`, and `overview_min_card_width` end to end.

tasks.title: The exposé is laggy with many panes — moving the cursor, and opening and closing it
tasks.description:
The exposé is laggy with many panes (26+ across 3 workspaces), worst on open/close and while moving the cursor.

═══ MEASURED 2026-08-19/20 — the guessing is over ═══
Instrumented per frame in a debug build with a many-pane session (`HECA_TRACE_PERF=1`):

    layout_layers   ~2.8–3.3 ms      <- every frame, whether or not anything moved
    frost blur      ~0.45 ms
    paint_layers    ~0.23 ms   (cmds=46–52)

`layout_layers` is about **four times the paint and the blur combined**, and it is rock-steady:
the cost does not vary with what the user is doing, because it is unconditional. In a 16.6 ms
budget at 60 fps that is a fifth of the frame before the panes, chrome or terminal are touched.

The second suspect named in the phase description — the frosted backdrop's full-screen blur — is
**not** the problem: 0.45 ms. Do not spend time on it.

`layout_layers` is `heca/src/chrome/mod.rs:1054`: a full `LayoutEngine::compute` over every visible
layer's root, each frame, with no dirty check.

═══ ATTEMPT 1 — REVERTED. Read this before designing attempt 2 ═══
A cache was added inside `LayoutEngine::compute` (record `(w, h, base_font, generation)` on the
root, skip while all four hold; the generation bumped by `mark_needs_paint`, since a tree has no
upward links). It was in the right place — the library, so every caller including a plugin benefits
— and it was **reverted immediately**: it broke the running app on startup. Pane borders detached
from their panes and drifted, and the pane header lost its title and its buttons.

**Why, exactly** (`heca/src/chrome/pane_header.rs:1090`): `sync_pane_headers` computes the header
and then calls `translate_tree(&mut header.root, x, y)` — mutating every widget's bounds AFTER the
pass, every frame. `compute` is therefore doing double duty: producing the layout **and resetting
the bounds to natural** so the next translate starts from a known place. Skip it and the translate
compounds frame after frame, and the header walks off screen.

**The premise was wrong, and that is the lesson.** "Layout is a pure function of the tree, its box
and its font" is false here: the host mutates retained trees between passes, and nothing declares
it. The measurement said WHERE the cost was; it did not say the work was skippable, and that was
treated as though it had.

`ScrollRegion` already solved the same problem the other way — its `on_layout` resets the baked
offset and re-applies it from scratch, so it is idempotent and a fresh pass cannot compound. That
is the shape to copy, not the flag to bolt on.

═══ THE OPTIONS — Antonio picks; do not choose one silently ═══

**A. Make placement idempotent, so skipping becomes safe.**
Replace `translate_tree`-after-compute with placement inside `Component::on_layout`, re-derived
from scratch each pass — exactly what `ScrollRegion` does today (`shift_subtree` + `on_layout`,
"a fresh layout pass would compound the shift, so on_layout resets and re-applies from scratch").
Then layout really is pure, the cache from attempt 1 works unchanged, and every caller benefits.
Cost: touches `sync_pane_headers`, the search bar (`chrome/mod.rs:1259` computes a tree then reads
its measured size back out) and `chrome/pane/shell.rs:193`. Aligns with the standing T400 note in
AGENTS.md — "bounds === what is drawn === what is clickable", floating panels become real placed
children. Biggest change, and the only one that removes the unstated contract rather than
documenting it.

**B. An explicit invalidation signal.**
`Base`/`LayoutEngine` gains "this tree was mutated out of band, re-run me", and every out-of-band
mutator calls it. Small diff. **But it is a rule every caller has to remember**, and a caller who
forgets gets silent stale bounds — the same class of failure as the deleted `routes_own_subtree` /
`takes_raw_keys` predicates, and the opposite of what Antonio has asked for repeatedly ("centralize
resolutions, do not just fix the call"). Recorded for completeness; it is the weakest option.

**C. Attack the COST, not the frequency — and measure it first.**
2.8 ms for one tree of ~26 panes is itself suspicious; taffy alone should not cost that. The prime
unmeasured suspect is **text measurement**: `measure_text_node` (heca-grid-ui/src/layout.rs) shapes
every label on every pass, and shaping is the expensive part. A shaping cache keyed on
`(text, font, constraints)` lives entirely inside the engine, needs **no contract change**, cannot
break any caller, and helps every layout in the app — not just layers.
**Do this measurement before choosing**: time `measure_text_node` separately from the taffy solve.
If shaping dominates, C alone may remove the problem and A becomes optional cleanup rather than a
prerequisite.

═══ NEXT STEP ═══
Split the 2.8 ms: how much is taffy solving, how much is text shaping. That single number decides
between C (cheap, safe, no contract change) and A (correct, larger, removes the unstated contract).
Instrumentation for the outer three passes is already in `heca/src/app/render.rs`, env-gated behind
`HECA_TRACE_PERF` — extend it inward rather than writing a new one.

═══ THE RULE THIS TASK KEEPS BREAKING ═══
Measure before fixing (the phase says so, and it has been right every time). But measuring where
the cost is is **not** the same as establishing that the work is unnecessary — attempt 1 conflated
the two and shipped a regression to Antonio's running app.

---
**Completion summary:**
CLOSED 2026-08-20 — NOT A BUG. Measured to nothing: the lag exists only in a debug build, and only with a pane count that never occurs while developing.

Antonio, 2026-08-20: "just run and in release mode there is no lag" · "while developing there will never be more than 4/5 panes so the problem does not exist. No need to optimize."

═══ WHAT WAS MEASURED ═══
Two rounds of per-frame instrumentation in a DEBUG build with 26 panes across 3 workspaces.

Round 1 — the three passes the phase named as suspects:
    layout_layers   ~2.8-3.3 ms   <- every frame, whether or not anything moved
    frost blur      ~0.45 ms
    paint_layers    ~0.23 ms  (cmds=46-52)
The frosted backdrop's full-screen blur — the phase's second suspect — was never the problem.

Round 2 — inside `LayoutEngine::compute`, splitting tree construction from the taffy solve:
    nodes=1514   build=1.5-1.9 ms   solve=22.5-23.6 ms   <- ONE tree, once per frame
    nodes=25     build=~26 us       solve=~270 us        <- x12, the pane headers
    nodes=2      build=~2 us        solve=~5 us          <- x12

Three findings, and the first two corrected earlier assumptions:

1. **The 1514-node tree is NOT a layer.** `layout_layers` accounted for only 2.8 ms, so the big
   cost comes from elsewhere — `paint_chrome_root` (the sidebar with every workspace, column and
   pane expanded), whose doc comment claims "Re-run every frame; cheap and creates no signals". At
   1514 nodes it is not cheap. Round 1 had been pointed at the wrong pass.
2. **Solve dominates build 15:1**, so keeping the taffy tree between passes would not have helped.
   The cost is taffy solving, not constructing nodes.
3. **`measure_text_node` shapes nothing** — it is arithmetic on a monospace advance ratio
   (`MONO_ADVANCE_RATIO`), so a text-shaping cache, the option that looked most attractive on
   paper, would have bought nothing either.

═══ WHY IT IS CLOSED ═══
Taffy is heavily generic, and unoptimised generics in a debug build routinely run 10-50x slower
than release. Antonio ran the same session in release: **no lag at all.** The 23 ms solve is a
debug-build artefact, not shipped behaviour.

And the debug case does not matter either: development happens with 4-5 panes, where the same tree
is a fraction of the size. A `[profile.dev.package."*"] opt-level = 2` line would have made even
the 26-pane debug case fast, and was declined as unnecessary — correctly, since nothing is slow in
the situation it would serve.

═══ THE ATTEMPT THAT WAS REVERTED — keep this, it is the real lesson ═══
Before the release measurement, a cache was added inside `LayoutEngine::compute` (record
`(w, h, base_font, generation)` on the root, skip while all four hold; the generation bumped by
`mark_needs_paint`, since a tree has no upward links). It was in the right PLACE — the library, so
every caller including a plugin would benefit — and it broke the running app on startup: pane
borders detached from their panes and drifted, and the pane header lost its title and its buttons.

Why exactly (`heca/src/chrome/pane_header.rs:1090`): `sync_pane_headers` computes the header and
then calls `translate_tree(&mut header.root, x, y)`, mutating every widget's bounds AFTER the pass,
every frame. `compute` is doing double duty — producing the layout AND resetting the bounds to
natural so the next translate starts from a known place. Skip it and the translate compounds frame
after frame, and the header walks off screen.

**"Layout is a pure function of the tree, its box and its font" is FALSE in this app**, because the
host mutates retained trees between passes and nothing declares it. `ScrollRegion` solved the same
problem the other way — its `on_layout` resets the baked offset and re-applies from scratch, so it
is idempotent and a fresh pass cannot compound. That is the shape to copy if this is ever revisited.

**The mistake worth remembering:** measuring WHERE the cost is is not the same as establishing that
the work is unnecessary. Round 1 was treated as though it had said both, and a regression shipped to
Antonio's running app.

═══ IF THIS EVER COMES BACK ═══
Real profiling in RELEASE first. If a cost is confirmed there, the recorded options were:
A. Make placement idempotent (`on_layout` re-derives, like `ScrollRegion`), so layout becomes pure
   and skipping is safe. Touches `sync_pane_headers`, the search bar (`chrome/mod.rs:1259`) and
   `chrome/pane/shell.rs:193`. Aligns with the T400 note in AGENTS.md — "bounds === what is drawn
   === what is clickable". The only option that removes the unstated contract rather than
   documenting it.
B. An explicit "this tree was mutated" signal every out-of-band mutator must call — small diff, but
   a rule every caller has to remember, and forgetting it gives silent stale bounds. Weakest.
C. Reduce the cost itself — ruled out above: build is 1/15 of solve, and text is not shaped.

Instrumentation has been removed. Nothing from this task remains in the tree.

⚠️ **This reverses a recorded decision** (`register`'s own comment: *"the remembered highlight wins because it is the more specific answer"*). Antonio reversed it — the map is a picture of **where you are**, so it opens where you are.

# FIXED 2026-08-13 — uncommitted on `feat/palette-modes`. ⏳ AWAITING ANTONIO'S DRIVE.

## The defect

`heca/src/chrome/expose/mod.rs`. The workspace was gated on whether the map was already up; **the pane was not** — `expose_cursor_per_ws[row]`, written by `record_expose_cursor` on every cursor move, won on a fresh open too. Open the map, arrow to another pane, dismiss, move nowhere: the next open started on the pane you browsed to while the session was still focused on the one you left, so the map drew its cursor on one card and its `active` styling on another.

## The fix

The resolution is now one **pure function**, `open_on(session, already_up, cursor_ws, cursor_per_ws) -> Option<PaneId>`, because it had been got wrong three times and could not be tested where it lived:

- **opening** → `session.active_workspace().active_pane()`. `active_pane()` answers for both domains — the focused float when one is active, the tiled pane otherwise — which is the same rule the model marks a card `active` by, so the cursor and the styling agree by construction;
- **rebuilding while up** → the remembered pane in the row the cursor is in, so a rebuild never moves the highlight (deleting a pane in one row must not jump the map to another — Antonio, 2026-08-11);
- a remembered pane that has since been **deleted** falls through to the session's focus.

It takes the `Session`, not the `AppState` around it, so all four answers are testable without a window.

## Tests (4, in `chrome/expose/mod.rs`)

- `opening_the_map_starts_on_the_pane_the_session_is_focused_on` — with a *different* pane remembered, and an assertion that the fixture really differs;
- `rebuilding_the_map_keeps_the_cursor_where_it_stands`;
- `a_rebuild_stays_in_the_row_the_cursor_is_in` — cursor in row 1 while the session is focused in row 0;
- `a_remembered_pane_that_no_longer_exists_falls_back_to_the_session`.

Workspace green, clippy 0 warnings.

# Verification (Antonio drives)

Focus a pane, open the map: the cursor is on it. Arrow away, Esc, open again: the cursor is back on the focused pane, not where you browsed. Then, with the map up, delete a card in a non-active row: the map stays in that row.

---
**Completion summary:**
**Verified by Antonio, 2026-08-13: *"works great."***

Shipped as the pure `open_on(session, already_up, cursor_ws, cursor_per_ws) -> Option<PaneId>` in `heca/src/chrome/expose/mod.rs`, with four tests covering opening, rebuilding, rebuilding in a non-active row, and a remembered pane that no longer exists. Uncommitted on `feat/palette-modes`.

tasks.title: Selection and cursor differ in KIND, not hue — a filled panel inside a glowing ring
tasks.description:
Found by Antonio driving the rebuilt exposé (T420), 2026-08-13: *"make the pane border color in the exposé different from the selected pane highlight. when we hover over the focused it's not easy to understand where the current focus is."*

# The defect

Two marks answer two different questions — **where the cursor is** versus **what is selected** — and `Row` draws them on the **same rectangle** (`Base::highlight_rect(SEL_INSET)`), the nav outline last. Both were an accent fill plus an accent edge, so the outline overwrote the active border and the two states became one exactly when they coincided. `DockFrame` had it identically (accent wash + accent ring), and **both carried a comment claiming the cursor was "a distinct colour"** — which the code had never done.

# Two failed attempts, and why hue could never fix it

1. **`foreground`** (honouring the old comment) — Antonio: *"still not distinguishable."*
2. **A dedicated amber `nav_cursor` token** — Antonio: *"orange is not a great color for tron legacy"*, and the same value was carried across three themes with different identities.

The reason hue cannot work, measured:

| theme | foreground | accent | glow |
|---|---|---|---|
| grid_tron | `#c6f0ff` | `#29b4fa` | `#29b4fa` |
| mocha | `#cdd6f4` | `#89b4fa` | `#89b4fa` |
| latte | `#4c4f69` | `#52679f` | `#52679f` |

`glow == accent` in all three and each foreground is a pale tint of it, so any borrowed token is a variation on the thing it must contrast with. Antonio's own proposal, `#012B37`, measured **1.33:1 against grid_tron's background** and 1.26:1 against its surface — a *surface* tone, invisible as a line.

# The fix — decided with Antonio, 2026-08-13

**They differ in KIND: selection is a FILL, the cursor is an EDGE.** A ring lets whatever is under it show through, so the cursor can sit on the selected row and both stay readable. Hue never has to carry the distinction again.

- **`Theme::selected_background: Option<Color>`** replaces the amber `nav_cursor`, with `effective_selected_background()` deriving it when unset: `surface.lerp(accent, 0.18)` — built from the theme's own two colours, so a user's theme gets a coherent selection without naming one.
- **`Row::paint`** — active draws the panel and **no border**; nav draws the accent ring + glow and **no fill** (`heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/row.rs`).
- **`DockFrame::paint`** — the active wash becomes the same panel; the cursor is the accent ring (`widgets/dock_frame.rs`). One rule for the whole library, which Antonio chose over a per-widget override.
- **The three `.highlight(theme.colors.accent)` call sites are gone** — `chrome/expose/pane_card.rs`, `providers/workspaces/mod.rs`, `examples/showcase.rs`. Forcing the accent as the highlight is what pinned the selection to the cursor's colour. `Row::highlight` survives for a genuinely state-tinted row.

## Per theme, in its own idiom (Antonio: *"latte is a light theme and mocha a dark alternative to tron"*)

| theme | selected panel | vs background | text on it | accent ring on it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| grid_tron | `#103d52` (surface lifted toward the cyan) | 1.71 | 9.56 | 4.97 |
| mocha | `#45475a` (Catppuccin Mocha Surface1) | 1.80 | 6.31 | 4.33 |
| latte | `#bcc0cc` (Catppuccin Latte Surface1 — **darker** than the page, as a light theme's selection must be) | 1.61 | 4.39 | 3.04 |

Workspace green, clippy 0 warnings. Uncommitted on `feat/palette-modes`.

# Verification (Antonio drives)

Exposé: move the cursor onto the pane that is already focused — a teal panel *inside* a neon ring, both readable. Sidebar: the same on a workspace frame and on a row. Then `prefix+Shift+r` after editing `selected_background` in a theme — it retunes without a rebuild.

---
**Completion summary:**
**VERIFIED across all three themes and COMMITTED as `e7f30ad`** (2026-08-13): *"now its perfect."*

# The rule that landed

Selection and the cursor are drawn on the **same rectangle**, so hue can never separate them — proven twice (accent, then foreground) before the shape changed. They differ in **kind**, and a container's hint is a third weight:

| weight | means | drawn as |
|---|---|---|
| faint wash (`active_wash_alpha`) | the current **workspace** | `DockFrame` active |
| opaque panel (`selected_background`) | the selected **row** | `Row` active |
| glowing accent ring | where the **cursor** is | `Row` / `DockFrame` nav |

⚠️ The first attempt painted the frame **and** the row at full strength, which cancelled exactly: a selected row inside the active workspace was the same colour as the frame around it, leaving only the column's marker bar. The container hint must stay a wash.

`Theme::selected_background: Option<Color>` + `effective_selected_background()` — derived as `surface.lerp(accent, 0.18)` when unset, so a user's own theme gets a coherent selection without naming one.

# Final per-theme values, each a step in its OWN palette

| theme | selected | vs frame wash | text on it | ring on it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| grid_tron | `#14506d` | 2.04 | 7.22 | 3.75 |
| mocha | `#585b70` (Surface2) | 1.75 | 4.62 | 3.17 |
| latte | `#cbd2e0` | 1.23 | 5.26 | 3.64 |

Latte took four rounds: the grey Catppuccin surface steps all read as *dark* on a light theme. It ended in the blue-grey family of `top_bottom_pane_background` (the pane header bar), one step darker than the header itself — on a light theme a selection is a tint toward the accent, not a step toward black.

# Also fixed in the same drive

- **The exposé card is a `surface`**, not `foreground` at 2%. A 2% wash is a tint for a card on a background you control; the map sits over a blurred photograph of the session, so what made a card visible was the theme's *glow* — grid_tron has one, mocha sets `glow_size = "none"` and its cards vanished entirely.
- **`Row`'s default marker is `ActiveMarker::None`**, matching `Item`. The bar was a second mark for one state, and beside `MarkerGroup`'s column bar it read as two lines. `providers/workspaces` dropped its explicit `.marker(Bar)` too.
- The three `.highlight(theme.colors.accent)` call sites are gone — forcing the accent as the highlight is what pinned selection to the cursor's colour.
